s: April 10, 2025 - First, sleep has established, independent associations with obesity and cardiometabolic health [4]. In 2022, the American Heart Association updated its Life’s Simple 7 to include sleep (thus becoming “Life’s Essential 8”), acknowledging its effect on cardiovascular health and relationship with other Simple 7 factors [2]. In an obesity context, a scoping review of international obesity management guidelines found that 34% incorporated sleep, demonstrating the growing recognition of sleep’s role [3]. Sleep can be addressed as a health behavior (e.g., sleep duration) or as a treated diagnosis (e.g., obstructive sleep apnea), and the increasing availability of accurate wearables for tracking sleep may make sleep assessments more feasible.
